quizzes.title: Key terms across the lectures
quizzes.intro: The vocabulary of managerial accounting, from cost object to break-even.

questions.q: Anything for which a separate measurement of cost is wanted is called
questions.explain: A cost object can be a product, an order, a machine or a department: whatever you want to know the cost of.

questions.q: Electricity for the whole dyeing hall, when the cost object is one dyeing order, is
questions.explain: It is shared by many orders and cannot be traced economically to one of them, so it is indirect and must be allocated.

questions.q: A cost that changes in total in proportion to the level of activity is
questions.explain: Variable costs move with the cost driver; fixed costs stay the same in total.

questions.q: Goods that have been started but are not yet complete are called
questions.explain: Work in process is the partly completed stock on the production floor.

questions.q: Unit selling price minus unit variable cost is the
questions.explain: UCM = USP − UVC: what each unit leaves to cover fixed cost and then profit.

questions.q: A cost can be direct for one cost object and indirect for another.
questions.explain: A loom-shed supervisor’s salary is direct to the weaving department but indirect to any single order woven there.

questions.q: Any factor whose change causes a change in the total cost of a cost object is
questions.explain: Units produced, machine set-ups and metres dyed are examples of cost drivers.

questions.q: The break-even point is the level of output at which
questions.explain: At break-even, profit is zero because revenue just covers variable plus fixed cost.

questions.q: Managerial accounting is prepared mainly for banks and the tax authority.
questions.explain: That describes financial accounting. Managerial accounting looks inwards and serves the decisions of managers.

questions.q: Asking how the break-even units change when fixed cost, variable cost or target profit change is called
questions.explain: Sensitivity analysis recalculates the answer for different “what if” values of the inputs.

quizzes.title: Linking the ideas
quizzes.intro: What happens to cost per unit, contribution and break-even when something changes.

questions.q: Production doubles while total fixed cost stays the same. Fixed cost per unit
questions.explain: The same total is spread over twice as many units, so the fixed cost per unit halves.

questions.q: Production doubles. The variable cost per unit
questions.explain: Total variable cost doubles with output, so the cost per unit is unchanged.

questions.q: If the selling price rises and nothing else changes, the break-even quantity
questions.explain: A higher price gives a larger contribution per unit, so fewer units are needed to cover fixed cost.

questions.q: If the yarn price paid by a weaving shed rises by Rs 1 a metre of fabric, the contribution per metre
options: Falls by the fixed cost per metre
questions.explain: Yarn is a variable cost, so every extra rupee of yarn cost comes straight off the contribution per metre.

questions.q: To find the units needed for a target profit, you divide by the unit contribution margin
questions.explain: Contribution must cover the fixed cost and then the profit wanted: (TFC + target profit) ÷ UCM.

questions.q: For a manufacturer, cost of goods sold is
options: Beginning finished goods + cost of goods manufactured − ending finished goods
Cost of goods manufactured + ending finished goods
questions.explain: Finished goods flow like any inventory: opening stock plus what was completed, less what is still unsold.

questions.q: In a commission dyeing plant the grey fabric is a variable cost of the dyer.
questions.explain: The fabric belongs to the customer. The dyer’s variable costs are dyes, chemicals and utilities.

questions.q: Depreciation of a pad-steam range, when the cost object is the dyeing department, is
questions.explain: The machine belongs wholly to that department (direct), and the charge does not change with metres dyed (fixed).

questions.q: Which change does NOT move the break-even point?
options: A fall in variable cost per unit
Selling more units than last month
questions.explain: Break-even depends on price, variable cost and fixed cost. Actual sales volume decides the profit, not where break-even lies.

questions.q: Total contribution margin minus total fixed cost equals operating profit.
questions.explain: Contribution first covers the fixed cost; whatever is left is profit.

quizzes.title: Mixed calculations
quizzes.intro: Unit cost, cost of goods manufactured and break-even, with fresh numbers.

questions.q: A product sells for Rs 250 and has a variable cost of Rs 160. Fixed cost is Rs 450,000 a month. How many units must be sold to break even?
For the same product (price Rs 250, variable cost Rs 160, fixed cost Rs 450,000), how many units give a profit of Rs 180,000?
A product sells for Rs 250 with a variable cost of Rs 160. What is the contribution margin ratio, in percent?
questions.explain: Contribution 90 ÷ price 250 = 36% of every sales rupee.

questions.q: Total cost for the month is Rs 1,800,000 for 45,000 metres. What is the unit cost per metre?
Fixed cost is Rs 600,000 a month. What is the fixed cost per unit at 20,000 units?
questions.explain: 600,000 ÷ 20,000 = Rs 30 per unit; at 40,000 units it would be half of that.

questions.q: Direct materials used Rs 760,000, direct labour Rs 180,000, indirect manufacturing cost Rs 110,000. Beginning work in process Rs 60,000, ending work in process Rs 70,000. Find the cost of goods manufactured.
questions.explain: Costs incurred 1,050,000 + beginning WIP 60,000 − ending WIP 70,000 = Rs 1,040,000.

questions.q: Cost of goods manufactured is Rs 1,040,000. Beginning finished goods are Rs 220,000 and ending finished goods Rs 180,000. Find the cost of goods sold.
A spinning mill has a fixed cost of Rs 360,000 a day. Yarn sells at Rs 52 per lb and raw material costs Rs 37 per lb. How many bags of 100 lb must it make each day to break even?
questions.explain: Contribution per bag = 15 × 100 = 1,500; 360,000 ÷ 1,500 = 240 bags a day.

questions.q: A loom has a daily fixed cost of Rs 4,200 and earns a contribution of Rs 8 per metre. How many metres a day must it weave to break even?
questions.explain: 4,200 ÷ 8 = 525 metres a day.

questions.q: A dyeing plant charges Rs 32 a metre; variable cost is Rs 20 a metre and fixed cost Rs 540,000 a day. What is the profit on a day when 50,000 metres are dyed?
questions.explain: Contribution = 12 × 50,000 = 600,000; less fixed cost 540,000 = Rs 60,000.

quizzes.title: Case study
quizzes.intro: A commission dyeing unit followed from its cost structure to its break-even and its response to change.

questions.q: What is the contribution per metre?
questions.explain: Charge 30 − variable cost 18 = Rs 12 per metre.

questions.q: How many metres a month must be dyed to break even?
What is the profit in a month when 55,000 metres are dyed?
What is the profit or loss in a month when only 35,000 metres are dyed? Enter a loss as a negative number.
What is the full cost per metre (variable plus fixed) when 48,000 metres are dyed in the month?
questions.explain: Fixed cost per metre = 480,000 ÷ 48,000 = 10; plus 18 variable = Rs 28.

questions.q: How many metres must be dyed to earn a profit of Rs 120,000 in a month?
Dye prices rise so that variable cost becomes Rs 20 a metre. What is the new break-even quantity?
questions.explain: Contribution falls to Rs 10; 480,000 ÷ 10 = 48,000 metres.

questions.q: With variable cost at Rs 20 a metre and the plant limited to 60,000 metres a month, the largest possible monthly profit is
questions.explain: At full capacity contribution = 10 × 60,000 = 600,000; less fixed cost 480,000 leaves Rs 120,000.

questions.q: For the cost object “one customer’s dyeing order”, the plant manager’s salary is
questions.explain: The salary is shared by all orders (indirect) and does not change with metres dyed (fixed).

questions.q: At the original costs, break-even uses two-thirds of the plant’s capacity.
questions.explain: Break-even is 40,000 metres and capacity is 60,000 metres: 40,000 ÷ 60,000 = two-thirds.

quizzes.case: A small dyeing unit dyes customers’ fabric for Rs 30 a metre. Dyes, chemicals and utilities cost Rs 18 a metre. Fixed costs (rent, salaries, depreciation) are Rs 480,000 a month. The plant can dye 60,000 metres a month.

quizzes.title: Group challenge
quizzes.intro: Harder questions that combine classification, unit cost and break-even.

questions.q: A stall sells juice at Rs 10 a glass, bought at Rs 6. The stall rent is Rs 5,000. If the rent rises to Rs 6,000 and the price to Rs 11, how many glasses are needed to break even?
questions.explain: New UCM = 11 − 6 = 5; 6,000 ÷ 5 = 1,200 glasses (it was 1,250 before).

questions.q: A weaving shed has 120 looms, each weaving 500 m a day. Contribution is Rs 9 a metre and the monthly fixed cost is Rs 14,400,000 (30 days). What is the profit per day for the whole shed?
questions.explain: Daily contribution = 60,000 × 9 = 540,000; daily fixed cost = 480,000; profit = Rs 60,000.

questions.q: In that shed (120 looms, 500 m per loom per day, daily fixed cost Rs 480,000), by how many rupees per metre can the contribution fall before the shed only breaks even?
questions.explain: Break-even contribution = 480,000 ÷ 60,000 = Rs 8 a metre, so the margin for error is 9 − 8 = Rs 1.

questions.q: A spinning mill makes 250 bags of 100 lb a day. Contribution is Rs 16 per lb and the daily fixed cost is Rs 380,000. What is the profit per month of 30 days?
Fixed cost is Rs 900,000 a month and variable cost Rs 40 a unit. What selling price gives break-even at exactly 30,000 units?
questions.explain: Price must cover variable cost plus fixed cost per unit: 40 + 900,000 ÷ 30,000 = Rs 70.

questions.q: Two products need the same machine time. A has a price of Rs 100 and variable cost Rs 70; B has a price of Rs 80 and variable cost Rs 45. With spare capacity for only one, which adds more profit per unit?
options: A, because its price is higher
B, because its contribution of Rs 35 is higher
A, because its variable cost is higher
questions.explain: Compare contributions: A leaves 30, B leaves 35. Price alone says nothing about what is left after variable cost.

questions.q: A mill’s unit cost was Rs 50 at 10,000 units and Rs 44 at 12,500 units, with no change in prices paid. The most likely reason is
options: Fixed cost was spread over more units
questions.explain: Unit cost falls with volume because the same fixed total is divided by more units.

questions.q: If a plant is running below its break-even output, selling one more unit at a price above variable cost still reduces the loss.
questions.explain: Every unit with a positive contribution pays for part of the fixed cost, even when total profit is still negative.

questions.q: Direct materials used = beginning inventory + purchases − ending inventory. If purchases are Rs 73,000, beginning inventory Rs 11,000 and materials used Rs 76,000, the ending inventory is
Selling price Rs 200, variable cost Rs 120, fixed cost Rs 1,000,000. Sales are 15,000 units. By how many units do sales exceed break-even (the margin of safety)?
